reasons.A: Closest movement and stance: short aphoristic turns ('She has simplified her possessions, very likely. She has not simplified her days.') set against longer dash-joined sentences, a wry, confiding irony ('Oh, I know the answer'), a 'Let us' cadence and rhetorical question answered with clipped 'Not...' fragments, all in period diction.
reasons.B: Good period feel with semicolon runs, 'one' constructions and a rhetorical question, but the semicolon list leans toward caricature, the contraction 'don't' and the flat 'My point is only this' break the register, and the tone argues more than it teases.
reasons.C: Plain modern exposition: even, declarative sentences, almost no semicolons, dashes or questions, no irony or allusive play, and a summarising close quite unlike the passage's paradoxical, epigrammatic manner.
